title: India's Amrit Vats and Pakistan's Muhammad Yahya Win Junior Doubles Title in Djibouti, Reviving Indo-Pak Express Memories
excerpt: The cross-border pair beat Thailand's David Avayou and Saudi Arabia's Ahmad Bahaa Sarouji 6-2, 6-4 to win the ITF World Tennis Tour Juniors J30 boys' doubles title in Djibouti.
body:
• India's Amrit Vats and Pakistan's Muhammad Yahya teamed up to win the boys' doubles title at the ITF World Tennis Tour Juniors J30 tournament in Djibouti.
  • The pair defeated Thailand's David Avayou and Saudi Arabia's Ahmad Bahaa Sarouji 6-2, 6-4 in the final.
  • Pakistan Tennis Federation president Aisam-ul-Haq Qureshi — one half of the original Indo-Pak Express — congratulated Yahya on the title.
  • The win recalls Rohan Bopanna and Qureshi's partnership, which reached the 2010 US Open final and won five ATP titles together.

Indian tennis player Amrit Vats and Pakistan's Muhammad Yahya have teamed up to win the boys' doubles title at the ITF World Tennis Tour Juniors J30 tournament in Djibouti, The Times of India reported. The pair defeated Thailand's David Avayou and Saudi Arabia's Ahmad Bahaa Sarouji 6-2, 6-4 in straight sets.

Pakistan Tennis Federation president Aisam-ul-Haq Qureshi congratulated Yahya on the achievement and praised his performance and sportsmanship, according to Pakistani reporting of the final. PTF secretary general Colonel Zia-ud-Din Tufail and other federation officials also extended their congratulations and best wishes for Yahya's international junior career.

A win that recalls the Indo-Pak Express

The partnership inevitably invites comparison with the most famous cross-border pairing in the sport's history. Rohan Bopanna and Aisam-ul-Haq Qureshi — the same Qureshi now congratulating Yahya — became one of tennis's most recognised doubles teams, earning the nickname "Indo-Pak Express." They reached the 2010 US Open men's doubles final, losing to the Bryan brothers, and won five ATP titles together, including the 2011 Paris Masters, along with tournaments in Dubai, Johannesburg, Halle and Stockholm. Both reached the top 10 in the doubles rankings.

Beyond results, Bopanna and Qureshi used their partnership to promote peace between India and Pakistan through their 'Stop War, Start Tennis' campaign, wearing specially designed T-shirts to spread the message. They received the Arthur Ashe Humanitarian of the Year award in 2010 for those efforts.

Why it resonates now

India and Pakistan have long shared a complicated relationship, and sport has often provided rare ground for cooperation. In recent years, political tensions have increasingly affected sporting ties between the two countries, making a junior doubles title won together — by a teenager from each side, at a tournament in East Africa — a small but genuine throwback to what the Bopanna-Qureshi years represented.

For Vats and Yahya, the immediate significance is ranking and experience: a J30 title is an early-career milestone on the ITF junior circuit, and winning it as an untested cross-border pairing, in straight sets, is the kind of result that gets young players noticed by coaches and federations on both sides.
